name: MIRTO Motifome Atlas
one_liner: A zero-backend static portal over the 889,215-instance human bilingual motifome: search any gene to read its 5'UTR / 3'UTR / protein sequence with motif highlights and per-nucleotide NTScore tracks, open any of the 900 motif clusters for its consensus, annotations and cross-modal partners, and explore the six protein-RNA meta modules as a live 519-node / 2,620-edge network — every byte precomputed into hash-routed JSON shards that will still load in five years from a plain file server.
stack:
BUILD (offline, one machine, no network): /opt/anaconda3/envs/bio/bin/python — verified present: pandas 2.3.3, pyarrow 21.0.0, numpy 1.26.4, h5py 3.11.0, scipy 1.15.3, igraph 0.11.6, networkx 3.3, logomaker 0.8.7, brotli 1.1.0, zstandard 0.25.0. STREME binary verified at /Users/wangyanz/software/meme/bin/streme (MEME 5.5.9) for the cluster-PWM gap fill. Pin these in code/build/requirements.txt. duckdb is NOT installed and is NOT required (see tradeoffs).

RUNTIME (browser, no toolchain — the user has zero package.json anywhere in the tree, so nothing may require npm/webpack/vite): hand-written ES2020 modules loaded with <script type="module">, no bundler, no transpile. Vendored (copied into the repo, NOT CDN-linked, so the site survives a CDN's disappearance): d3-selection 3.0.0, d3-zoom 3.0.0, d3-scale 4.0.2, d3-shape 3.2.0, d3-force 3.0.0 (only for the optional "re-simulate" button; layout ships frozen), d3-array 3.2.4 — ~120 KB minified total; pako 2.1.0 (~45 KB) as the fallback gunzipper where DecompressionStream('gzip') is unavailable. Nothing else. No React, no Plotly (the user's 9.56 MB Plotly-inlined prototype at sequence_analysis_v3_0515/04.visualize_motif_interaction/annotated_interacting_protein_utr3.html is the anti-pattern this replaces), no Tailwind, no web components.

RENDERING: hand-rolled SVG for logos, tracks, dot plots and the network; canvas 2D for exactly two things (the 180,000-point Fig 3c UMAP and the per-line NTScore strips); plain DOM for sequence text so it stays selectable and copyable.

STYLING: one CSS file with custom properties. Three-state theme block lifted verbatim from /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/manuscript/results_code_mapping_index/03.panel_code_index.html (:root / @media(prefers-color-scheme:dark){:root:not([data-theme="light"])} / :root[data-theme="dark"]). Palette tokens transcribed from /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/manuscript/main_figures_code/_shared/manuscript_style.py into code/portal/theme.json + CSS vars: modules M1 #0072B2, M2 #CC79A7, M3 #E69F00, M4 #D55E00, M5 #4D4D4D, M6 #009E73 (the MCOL dict used identically by four published figure scripts — NOT the CATEGORICAL-cycle variant in motif_umap/make_individual_figures.py, and NOT the unimplemented proposal in _shared/COLOR_TABLE.md); regions utr5 #E69F00, utr3 #A85A00, protein #0072B2; nucleotides A #009E73, C #0072B2, G #E69F00, U/T #D55E00; amino acids from examples_lib.aacol(). Typography from the same GEN-2 report: Newsreader headings / Source Sans 3 body / JetBrains Mono sequence — self-hosted WOFF2 in the repo, no Google Fonts request (a font CDN is another 5-year liability), with system-stack fallbacks.

HOSTING: static files only. Hash-based routing (#/gene/ACTB) so no server rewrite rules, no .htaccess, no 404 fallback config are needed — this is the single choice that makes the site portable between GitHub Pages, an Apache lab server, an S3 bucket and a Zenodo-deposited zip unzipped on a laptop.
architecture:
DATA FLOW: parquet/h5/csv/pkl on the author's disk → one idempotent Python build → a self-contained directory of gzipped JSON shards + a small app → browser fetch + client-side decompress + hand-rolled render. Nothing is computed at request time and nothing is queried at request time.

STAGE 1 — BAKE (python, ~6-8 min wall, absolute input paths confined to this stage).
  Reads the master table motif_full_annotations.parquet (889,215 x 24), the sequence table GRCh37_latest_rna_sequence_pairs_long_transcript.parquet (deduplicated on refseq_id_without_ver: 21,667 -> 19,210 rows, verified lossless), the two NTScore HDF5 caches, the v4 module/edge CSVs, the figure3_4 intermediate caches, and annotation_coverage_stats.json. Writes code/portal/data/.
  Every path is declared once in code/build/paths.py. The emitted site reads only relative paths — the "absolute inputs, relocatable outputs" convention every figure3_4 README already states.

STAGE 2 — STATIC TREE (measured sizes, gzip -9):
  data/index/symbols.json.gz            0.157 MB  17,847 symbols -> [refseq, n_motifs]
  data/index/ids.json.gz                0.26  MB  18,093 RefSeq + 20,481 ENSG + 20,481 ENST -> refseq (lazy, loaded on first non-symbol query)
  data/index/excluded.json.gz          ~0.03  MB  1,117 motif-free RefSeq ids + reason
  data/gene/<REFSEQ>.json.gz           63.6   MB  18,093 files, mean 3.51 KB, p90 7.0 KB, p99 10.4 KB, max 11.4 KB
  data/ann/<REFSEQ>.json.gz            12.3   MB  18,093 files, mean 0.68 KB, max 2.1 KB (region-filtered annotations)
  data/cluster/<CLUSTER>.json.gz       17.9   MB  900 files, mean 19.9 KB, p90 25.9 KB, max 58.3 KB
  data/net/*.json.gz                   ~1.6   MB  nodes, edges, meta_edges, consensus_meta, cluster_index, carrier lists
  data/module/M{1..6}.json.gz          ~0.75  MB  GO (trusted + all), gene lists, validation payloads
  data/pairs/umap.bin + meta.json.gz    1.0   MB  quantized uint16 xy + uint16 npmi + uint8 module for 180,000 pairs
  data/pairs/all_pairs.json.gz          1.93  MB  180,000 x 9 trimmed columns (lazy, only for the pair explorer)
  app shell (html+css+js+fonts+d3)     ~0.35  MB  ESTIMATE, not measured
  TOTAL ~= 100 MB gzipped, ~36,900 files. GitHub Pages soft limits are 1 GB published / 100 GB month bandwidth.

STAGE 3 — RUNTIME. index.html loads app.js (router) + theme.css + symbols.json.gz. Router parses location.hash, resolves the view module, which fetches only the shards it needs through one loader:
  async function shard(path){ const r = await fetch(path); const buf = 'DecompressionStream' in self ? await new Response(r.body.pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('gzip'))).arrayBuffer() : pako.ungzip(await r.arrayBuffer()); return JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(buf)); }
  An LRU Map caches the last ~40 shards in memory; the HTTP cache does the rest. Pre-gzipping (rather than shipping plain .json and trusting the host) is deliberate: it guarantees the 4.6x transfer saving on a lab Apache box that sets no Content-Encoding, at the cost of ~30 lines of loader.

MEASURED PER-ACTION COST: first paint 0.35 MB (shell) + 0.157 MB (symbol index) + ~0.04 MB (home payload) ~= 0.35-0.55 MB. Gene lookup 3.5 KB median / 10.4 KB p99 / 11.4 KB max, plus 0.68 KB if the annotation drawer is opened. Cluster open 19.9 KB median / 58.3 KB max. Network view 1.6 MB once, then free. Pair explorer +1.0 MB once. Compare: a per-gene query against the source parquet as it exists today costs 18.25 MB because all three parquets are written as a SINGLE row group, and 0.21 MB even after re-sorting and re-chunking to row_group_size=8000.

ROUTING (hash only — no server config):
  #/                       home / search
  #/gene/ACTB              resolves symbol -> RefSeq; #/tx/NM_001101 addresses a transcript directly
  #/gene/ACTB?r=utr3&pos=82&m=utr3_0313   deep link to a region, scroll position and selected motif
  #/cluster/utr3_0215      #/cluster/utr3_0215?tab=partners|members|annotations
  #/pair/prot_0038~utr3_0215   an edge detail
  #/module/M4              #/module/M4?tab=go|genes|network|validation
  #/network?view=featured|full|M4&score=0.3&cross=1
  #/pairs                  Fig 3c explorer
  #/evidence  #/methods  #/isoforms  #/about
Every panel writes its state into the hash, so any view a reader reaches is a URL they can paste into the paper's supplementary text.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: module_term_gene_long.csv (27 MB), module_trusted_term_gene_long.csv (12.9 MB), protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv in full 15-column form (18 MB), cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz raw (13 MB), motif_rbp_overlaps.parquet (58 MB), either source parquet, either NTScore h5 (169 + 119 MB), the mouse motifome, and the 9.5 MB Plotly prototypes.

views.title: Search & overview
views.purpose: Answer the two questions a first-time visitor has — 'what is this?' and 'does my gene have anything?' — inside one screen, and make the six modules and the corpus scale legible before any click.
components: six module cards with mini bipartite glyph and ZNF risk figure
footer with DOI, manuscript link, panel map
interactions: type-ahead fires on every keystroke against the in-memory symbol index (17,847 entries, 0.157 MB) with prefix-then-substring ranking; arrow keys + Enter navigate
pasting an ENSG/ENST/NM id lazily pulls ids.json.gz and resolves to one RefSeq (verified 1:1 in the search direction)
a symbol with >1 transcript (215 genes, max 7 for BAG6) expands inline into a transcript chooser instead of guessing
a symbol that exists only in the excluded list (e.g. TTN) routes to the excluded empty state, not to 'no results'
example chips deep-link to #/gene/<sym>?m=<cluster> so the named motif is pre-selected and scrolled to
module card click -> #/module/M<n>; module glyph hover previews the module's top pair
coverage bar hover shows numerator/denominator/percent from annotation_coverage_stats.json
views.entry_points: The site root and the URL printed in the manuscript. Leaves to #/gene/<sym>, #/module/M<n>, #/network, #/cluster/<id> (via the browse card), #/about, #/evidence. Reachable from every other view via the masthead logo and the always-present search field in the header.

Each region panel has two modes. TRACK mode: the whole region on one horizontal axis, NTScore as a canvas area chart, motifs as SVG rects, letters appear only past ~1.5 px/nt — this is the only mode that works for a 7,601 nt 3'UTR. READ mode: 60 nt per wrapped line in JetBrains Mono, motif spans as bordered <span> elements inside the text so selection and copy still work, with a 60-px-wide canvas NTScore strip above each line, lines mounted lazily by IntersectionObserver. 5'UTR defaults to read mode (median 186 nt), 3'UTR to track mode (median 1,062 nt), protein to read mode (median 401 aa).

+------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. THE ARITHMETIC                                          |
|   18,068 genes  ->  effective N 2,342 (13.0%)              |
|   |###############################|                        |
|   547 ZNF genes ->  effective 9.0 (1.7%)                   |

views.title: How this was built & glossary
views.purpose: Let a reader who arrives from the paper understand, without leaving the site, what a motif is here, what the four nested motif objects are, and exactly which thresholds produced the network.
views.layout:
Sticky pill nav + step cards, reusing the layout idiom of MODULE_IDENTIFICATION_WALKTHROUGH.html (43fr prose / 57fr detail grid).

+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| [1 model] [2 motifs] [3 clusters] [4 pairs] [5 modules] [glos] |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| flowbar:  mRNA+protein -> NTScore -> delta-attention ->        |
|           motif instances -> clusters -> NPMI+APC ->           |
|           phylo gate -> Louvain -> M1..M6                      |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| HIERARCHY (live counts, each number is a link)                 |
|   instance          889,215   ->  a row; one substring         |
|   unique_motif_id   577,186   ->  a string, NOT an instance    |
|   motif_cluster         900   ->  300 prot / 500 utr3 / 100 u5 |
|   consensus (cid)     1,226   ->  over 451 clusters only       |
|   module                  6   ->  covers 513 of 900 clusters   |
|   ! 34,110 unique_motif_ids (5.91%) sit in >1 cluster.         |
|     'CTGGA' alone spans 176 clusters. Cluster is a property    |
|     of the instance's context, never of the string.            |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| THE GATE (verbatim)                                           |
|   clade_concentration < 0.35 AND n_indep_clades >= 8 AND       |
|   npmi_mip_APC > 0.10 AND co_count >= 10                       |
|   weight = MIp x (1 - clade_concentration) x log1p(clades)     |
|   Louvain modularity 0.47, 9 communities, 6 retained           |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| GLOSSARY cards: NTScore, SeqScore, SpecScore, delta-attention, |
|   NPMI, APC/MIp, phylogenetic independence, module, carrier    |
|   gene, trusted term, coverage, carriers, pLDDT                |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+

diagram is exportable as SVG for slides

data_pipeline:
One idempotent Python package at /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/manuscript/online_contents/code/build/, run as `python -m build all` with /opt/anaconda3/envs/bio/bin/python. All absolute input paths live in build/paths.py and nowhere else; all outputs are written under code/portal/data/ with relative names. Total wall time ~7 min (plus an optional ~15 min STREME fill). 00_validate.py — hard assertions that fail the build loudly rather than shipping silently wrong highlights. - seq[motif_start:motif_end+1] == motifs for all 889,215 rows (the survey's s05_full.py, adopted verbatim; runs in 0.5 s). - motif_length == motif_end - motif_start + 1 for 100% of rows. - motif_end < len(region sequence) for all rows (0 overruns). - max interval stacking depth == 1 in every (sequence_id, region) group. - drop_duplicates('refseq_id_without_ver') on the sequence table is lossless (all 1,296 duplicate groups byte-identical). - all 18,093 motif sequence_ids join to the sequence table. - the 8 published annotation coverage percentages reproduce exactly under the `applies` mask (the survey's s18_verify_filter.py, kept as a regression test). - NTScore array length == region sequence length for every transcript in both h5 files. (I verified 200/200 sampled for each region; the build asserts all 18,093.) - motif_cluster == f'{prefix}_{kmeans_label:04d}' with a region-consistent prefix, 0 mismatches. 01_core_tables.py — loads motif_full_annotations.parquet (889,215 x 24), the deduplicated sequence table (19,210 rows), modules.json, protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv, phylo_corrected_candidates.csv, cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz, consensus_meta.csv, consensus_repertoire.pkl, consensus_pair_scores.csv.gz, consensus_presence.npz, cluster_term_labels.csv, interpro_entry_map.csv, annotated_protein_sequences.csv, idmapping_2026_05_08.tsv, annotation_coverage_stats.json, motif_genome_mappings_grch37.parquet. Builds the canonical cluster table (900 rows: cluster, region, kmeans_label, module_or_null, n_instances, n_genes, n_unique_motif_ids, display_name, name_tier, top consensus, coverage, positional histogram, length/score/entropy/pLDDT quantiles, composition) — the single derived artifact every view reads, so the four drifting copies in the figure tree are never consulted at runtime. 02_annotations.py — rebuilds the annotation layer ID-bearing and region-correct: re-joins overlapping_interpro_labels from 01.interpro/motif_interpro_annotations.parquet, idpo_ids from 05.idpo/motif_idpo_annotations.parquet, the UniProt Entry from 06.mobidb/motif_mobidb_annotations.parquet, and typed UniProt features recomputed from 03.uniprot/uniprot_annotation.parquet with the 0-based-corrected overlap rule (~756,192 hits, ~2 min). Applies the `applies` mask from annotation_coverage_stats.json, dropping 209,959 spurious MobiDB, 1,825 IDPO and 665 SignalP UTR rows. Never comma-splits interpro/uniprot/elm. Applies the RBP alias map. Output: an in-memory annotation frame keyed on raw_motif_index. 03_ntscore.py — reads outputs_utr3_score_0318.h5 (18,585 keys) and outputs_utr5_score_0326.h5 (18,093 keys), asserts per-transcript length alignment, quantizes 'score' to uint8 over a fixed [-8.0, 0.0] domain (measured range over 400 transcripts: min -7.0, max -0.0016; the build recomputes the true global min and fails if it falls outside the domain), base64-encodes and emits into each gene shard. MEASURED: mean 1,871 B gz per transcript, p90 4,173, p99 6,010, max 6,944 -> 33.9 MB total. 04_gene_shards.py — writes 18,093 x data/gene/.json.gz {t, g, ensg[], enst[], s{u5,u3,p}, n{u5,u3}, m{utr5[],utr3[],protein[]}, dom[], flags{}} and 18,093 x data/ann/.json.gz. MEASURED on a 400-transcript sample: core mean 3,514 B gz (p50 2,763, p90 7,038, p99 10,377, max 11,353) -> 63.6 MB; annotations mean 681 B (p50 594, p90 1,235, max 2,148) -> 12.3 MB. Also emits data/index/symbols.json.gz (0.157 MB), data/index/ids.json.gz (~0.26 MB), data/index/excluded.json.gz (the 1,117 motif-free transcripts with reason and length; 666 exceed the 7,784 nt context cap). 05_streme_fill.py (OPTIONAL, run once) — closes the biggest content gap. STREME PWMs exist for only 466 of 900 clusters because the pipeline was only ever run on the 513 module clusters. Reuses windows_fasta() / run_streme() / parse_streme() / coverage() from motif_pair_network/16_consensus_repertoire.py verbatim so new matrices are method-identical: `streme --p --n background_sequences_{region}.fasta --oc --nmotifs 12` plus `--protein --minw 6 --maxw 15` or `--rna --minw 5 --maxw 12`, discovery FASTA filtered to motif_length>=5, capped at 1,200 sorted by motif_score desc, RNA T->U. Measured cost 64.3 s per protein cluster, 5-10 s per UTR cluster -> ~2.4 CPU-hours, ~15 min at WORKERS=10. Expect ~100-150 protein clusters to still return nothing significant; those get the composition fallback. 06_cluster_shards.py — writes 900 x data/cluster/.json.gz {cluster, region, module, name, name_tier, stats, consensus[], pwm[], pos_hist[20], enrichment[] (de-duplicated on (cluster, source, display) keeping min fdr_cluster, top ~40 rows), freq{} (instance-level annotation frequency), partners{strict[],relaxed[]}, members[]}. MEASURED on a 60-cluster sample with the full member list and the frequency aggregates: mean 19,877 B gz (p50 18,490, p90 25,872, max 58,295) -> 17.9 MB for all 900. (A top-200-member variant measures 5,019 B mean / 4.5 MB total if the budget ever needs it; not needed at 17.9 MB.) Also emits data/net/cluster_index.json.gz (~150 KB: all 900 clusters with region, module, name, counts, top consensus, and the 4-dp PWM bundle for the 451+ clusters that have one). 07_network.py — expands modules.json into the cluster->module map (513 of 900); builds data/net/nodes.json.gz (519 nodes with frozen x/y from a one-off igraph bipartite+module-blocked layout, module block order from a port of node_select.order_modules()), data/net/edges.json.gz (2,620 rows x 15 cols, 89 KB gz, plus mp/mu module ids and the UMAP xy joined from cca_winner_umap.npy), data/net/meta_edges.json.gz (the 6x6 cross-module matrix, which exists nowhere on disk: M1-M2 244, M1-M5 192, M2-M3 167, M1-M6 32, M1-M3 30, M2-M5 28, M3-M4 22, M5-M6 15, M3-M6 6, M2-M4 5, M2-M6 5, M3-M5 5, M4-M5 4, M1-M4 1, M4-M6 1), data/net/consensus_pairs.json.gz (top 3 per covered edge, ~3,599 rows / 703 KB), data/net/relaxed_edges.json.gz (the 7,210 npmi_mip_APC>0.1 superset, trimmed), and data/net/carriers/

~.json.gz (shared carrier gene lists precomputed by bitwise AND of Pc and Uc columns of consensus_presence.npz over its 18,068 RefSeq ids, mapped to symbols). 08_modules.py — writes data/module/M{1..6}.json.gz: header statistics from modules.json/modules_summary.csv, GO from module_GO_enrichment.csv split into all-significant and trusted (q<0.05 AND fold>=2 AND n_fam_support>=5; 3,530 of 6,389 rows), GO_term_specificity.csv, the member gene table from module_gene_index.csv with the trusted_terms text column truncated to a count plus a lazy tail, term->gene lists from module_term_gene_lists.csv (2.2 MB source, split per module), and the module-specific validation payloads (m1_m2_rbp_enrichment.csv, m1_m2_apex_localization.csv, utr_composition.csv, motif_2x2_kinetics_summary.csv, tls_nuclear_degradation_M5.csv, ribomap_validation.csv, M6_utr5_0004_GCCGCCACC_kozak_genes.csv). ~0.75 MB total. 09_pairs.py — quantizes cca_winner_umap.npy (180000 x 2 float32) to uint16 over its bounding box (max error 0.000234 units), emits data/pairs/umap.bin (xy) + npmi.bin (uint16) + module.bin (uint8) = 0.994 MB gz, plus a 128x128 bucket index for hover, plus data/pairs/all_pairs.json.gz (protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv trimmed to 9 columns, 1.93 MB gz). Records the v3-tree source path and mtime in the manifest because nothing in the v4 pipeline regenerates it. 10_static.py — copies the app shell, vendored d3 submodules and pako, self-hosted WOFF2 fonts, theme.json (transcribed from _shared/manuscript_style.py), glossary.json, and the verbatim caveat/methods text extracted from MODULES_REPORT.md, REPORT.md, relatedness_report.md and module_gene_members/README.md. 11_manifest.py — writes data/manifest.json: snapshot version, ISO build timestamp, and for every input file its absolute path, size, mtime and SHA-256; plus the emitted file inventory with sizes. Prints the total and fails if it exceeds a configured budget (default 150 MB). TOTAL OUTPUT: ~100 MB gzipped across ~36,900 files. Rebuild is fully deterministic given the same inputs, so the manifest is a real provenance record rather than a decoration.

phases.exit_criteria: `python -m build validate` passes all nine assertions on the full 889,215 rows, reproduces all 8 published annotation coverage percentages exactly, and prints the canonical cluster table with 900 rows / 513 module-assigned / 463 with a significant term / 466 with a PWM. No UI work has started.

phases.name: P1 - R1 gene view
phases.deliverable: 03_ntscore.py + 04_gene_shards.py emitting 18,093 core and 18,093 annotation shards plus the search indexes; the app shell (router, loader with DecompressionStream+pako, theme, caveat ribbon); the home view; the gene view with all three region panels in both track and read mode, NTScore tracks, motif span lanes, minimap, filter bar, motif detail rail, annotation chips, all-motifs table, three empty states and exports.
phases.exit_criteria: ACTB (NM_001101) shows exactly 3 5'UTR, 13 3'UTR and 4 protein motifs; all three 5'UTR motifs are in utr5_0004; the 45-nt AU-rich 3'UTR element at 82-126 shows TIAL1 among its eCLIP RBPs; no 5'UTR or 3'UTR motif anywhere displays a MobiDB/IDPO/SignalP term; UTRs display in RNA alphabet; searching TTN returns the excluded-transcript state naming the 7,784 nt context cap; the longest 3'UTR in the corpus (7,601 nt) renders in track mode without jank; gene lookup transfers <= 11.4 KB.

phases.name: P5 - Snapshot, deploy, cite
phases.deliverable: A tagged snapshot v1.0.0 with manifest.json, a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the build and force-pushes only the built directory to an orphan gh-pages branch (so the ~36,900 shard files never enter the main branch's history), a Zenodo deposit of the built directory with a concept DOI, the citation block on #/about, and a short USAGE.md covering offline use via `python -m http.server`.
phases.exit_criteria: The site loads from the published URL with a first paint under 600 KB and a gene page under 400 ms on a cold cache; the same directory unzipped locally and served with python -m http.server behaves identically; the DOI resolves; the repository sits under a lab or institutional GitHub organisation, not a personal account; a fresh clone plus one build command reproduces the published site byte-for-byte apart from the timestamp.

tradeoffs:
STATIC SHARDS vs DUCKDB-WASM OVER RANGE-REQUESTED PARQUET — decided by measurement, not taste. All three source parquets are written as a SINGLE row group, so predicate pushdown prunes nothing and a per-gene range-request query would fetch 18.25 MB. Re-sorting by gene_symbol and rewriting at row_group_size=8000 brings that to 0.21 MB for a 24% file-size increase — still ~60x more bytes than the 3.5 KB shard, on top of a 3-5 s WASM cold start, a ~1.2 MB runtime download, an HTTP-Range requirement that a plain lab Apache config may not honour, and a query engine to keep working for five years. DuckDB is not even installed on the author's machine. The only capability it would buy is arbitrary user-composed SQL across all 889,215 rows, which none of R1/R2/R3 asks for; the specific cross-cutting queries that matter (all members of a cluster, all partners of a cluster, all genes in a module, all carriers of an edge) are precomputed into shards at build time. Verdict: no WASM, no query engine, no re-partitioning. If arbitrary querying is ever demanded, add a FastAPI+DuckDB service behind the same static frontend rather than replacing it.

PLAIN .json vs PRE-GZIPPED .json.gz — chose pre-gzipped with a DecompressionStream loader. Plain JSON is simpler and GitHub Pages would gzip it in transit, but a lab Apache or a Zenodo-unzipped local copy may set no Content-Encoding, and the 4.6x difference is the difference between a 3.5 KB and a 16 KB gene fetch. The cost is ~30 lines of loader plus a 45 KB pako fallback. Documented as a build flag so a future maintainer can flip it.

PER-GENE FILES vs BUCKETED SHARDS — chose one file per gene (18,093 files) over ~256 hash buckets. Buckets would cut the file count 70x but make every gene lookup fetch ~180 KB instead of 3.5 KB. The cost is a repository with ~36,900 small files, which makes `git clone` slow; mitigated by generating shards in CI and force-pushing only the built tree to an orphan branch, so the shards never accumulate history.

SEQUENCE AS DOM TEXT vs CANVAS — chose DOM. Canvas would be faster for a 7,601 nt 3'UTR but would destroy text selection, copy, find-in-page and screen-reader access, which for a sequence portal is the whole point. The measured segment counts make DOM viable: motifs never overlap (max stacking depth exactly 1 across all 53,367 transcript-region groups), so a flat alternation of text nodes and spans needs at most 381 elements (median 89). The compromise is the two-mode design: track mode (canvas score + SVG rects, no letters) for overview, read mode (DOM letters, lazily mounted 60 nt per line) for detail.

SVG NETWORK vs CANVAS/WEBGL — chose SVG for the 519-node / 2,620-edge graph and canvas only for the 180,000-point UMAP. At network scale SVG gives per-element hit-testing, CSS hover, keyboard focus and an export-to-publication path for free; the click-for-details requirement would otherwise need hand-rolled hit-testing. At UMAP scale SVG is impossible and canvas plus a build-time spatial bucket grid is the only sane choice.

FROZEN LAYOUT vs LIVE FORCE SIMULATION — chose frozen, with an optional re-simulate button. A live simulation settles differently on every load, so deep links to a region of the graph and any resemblance to published Fig 3e are lost. The cost is that the frozen layout will not exactly reproduce Fig 3e (which came from a min-linear-arrangement inside a matplotlib script); the portal will look like a sibling of the figure, not a clone, and the 'featured (as published)' 52-node view exists to bridge that.

FULL MEMBER LISTS vs TOP-N IN CLUSTER SHARDS — chose full. Measured full-member cluster shards are 19.9 KB mean / 58.3 KB max versus 5.0 KB for a top-200 cap. Truncating a cluster's members would silently hide up to 5,555 instances of utr3_0188, which is exactly the kind of quiet omission a resource should not make. 17.9 MB total is affordable.

ONE TRANSCRIPT PER GENE — accepted, because the motif table has exactly one (essentially the longest) per gene. The portal states the transcript on every gene page and confines isoform comparison to a fixed case-study page for the five genes with isoform data, rather than shipping an isoform selector that would be empty for 18,088 of 18,093 genes.

HUMAN ONLY — dropped mouse for v1. A parallel 827,161-instance mouse motifome exists and annotation_coverage_stats.json is already species-keyed, but mouse any-annotation coverage is 25.3% versus 63.9% and including it roughly doubles the build and the payload. The shard path scheme reserves data/<species>/ so mouse is an additive change.

DESIGN STORY (Fig 5/6, SOX2) — dropped from v1. It serves a different audience (mRNA engineers) from a different data tree; folding it in would double the scope before R1/R2/R3 are complete. Flagged as a scope question for the author.

STRICT TIER AS DEFAULT — chose the manuscript's own 2,620-edge gate as the default everywhere, with the 7,210-edge npmi>0.1 superset behind an explicit labelled toggle, and npmi_raw available as a sort key only behind a warning. This means 282 of 600 UTR clusters open with an empty partner table; that empty state is designed content explaining the gate, not a failure. Silently relaxing the threshold to fill pages would misrepresent the paper's central statistical claim and would reproduce the artifact leaderboard the analysis exists to remove.
risks: MANUSCRIPT/DATA CONFLICT, BLOCKING THE M2 EXAMPLE: the manuscript says 'MLXIPL ... contains the M2 utr3_0027 motifs (Fig. 4a)', but modules.json assigns utr3_0027 to module 1 while the code that actually produced Fig 4a (build_mlxipl_signatures.py, MLXIPL_M2_signatures.csv) uses utr3_0227, which is module 2. Every data file agrees with utr3_0227. This is almost certainly a one-character typo, but the portal will publicly expose the inconsistency on the M2 landing card whichever way it is built. One question to the author; it blocks nothing else, and the portal should build on utr3_0227 in the meantime.

SEARCHING A FAMOUS EXCLUDED GENE CANNOT NAME IT: 1,117 transcripts have no motifs (666 because they exceed the model's 7,784 nt context cap, the largest being TTN), and the sequence table has no gene_symbol column. I checked idmapping_2026_05_08.tsv directly: it covers 0 of those 1,117 RefSeq ids, so no local file can map them to symbols. Without an external RefSeq->symbol source (NCBI gene2refseq, or one offline mygene call for 1,117 ids, producing ~30 KB of JSON) a search for TTN is indistinguishable from a typo. Small, but it is the first thing a sceptical reader will try.

HALF THE CLUSTER PAGES ARE THIN UNLESS THE STREME FILL IS RUN AND EVEN THEN MAY STAY THIN: STREME PWMs exist for 466 of 900 clusters and 437 of 900 clusters have no term at FDR<0.05 — 229 clusters have neither. The fill is cheap (~2.4 CPU-hours, binary verified present) but a measured fresh run on prot_0002 (976 sequences, 64.3 s) returned 12 motifs and 0 significant, so an estimated 100-150 protein clusters will still have no logo afterwards. The composition fallback is honest but visually weaker, and the three clusters the manuscript features most (utr5_0090, utr5_0096, utr3_0215) are in the no-significant-term set.

THE ANNOTATION REGION LEAK IS A ONE-LINE REGRESSION AWAY FROM A VISIBLE SCIENTIFIC ERROR: MobiDB is populated on 67.0% of 5'UTR and 25.3% of 3'UTR rows with protein-disorder terms (209,959 spurious rows, plus 1,825 IDPO and 665 SignalP) because those builders never filtered region=='protein'. If the `applies` mask ever regresses, the portal will tell RNA biologists that a 3'UTR nucleotide motif has intrinsic protein disorder. The build-time regression test against the 8 published coverage numbers is the only thing standing between the site and that error, and it must not be allowed to become optional.

NTSCORE QUANTIZATION DOMAIN IS NOT ESTABLISHED GLOBALLY: I measured the score range over 400 random transcripts (min -7.0, max -0.0016) and chose a [-8, 0] uint8 domain, but no survey established the true global minimum across all 18,093 transcripts and both regions. If any transcript falls below -8 the track will clip silently. The build must compute the true global min/max and fail if the domain is wrong; this is a two-line fix but an easy one to skip.

PRE-GZIPPED SHARDS DEPEND ON DecompressionStream OR PAKO: DecompressionStream('gzip') is broadly available but not universal, some corporate proxies rewrite or strip binary responses, and a misconfigured host may serve .json.gz with a Content-Encoding header that causes double decompression. The pako fallback covers the first case; the third needs a documented host check. The alternative (plain .json, host-side compression) is a build flag but quadruples the transfer on a host that compresses nothing.

REPOSITORY HYGIENE AND URL SURVIVAL, NOT TECHNOLOGY, ARE THE REAL FIVE-YEAR RISKS: ~36,900 small files make a naive git clone slow, and a GitHub Pages URL under a personal account dies when that account is renamed, deleted, or the student leaves. The mitigation (build in CI, force-push only the built tree to an orphan branch, host under a lab or institutional organisation, mint a Zenodo DOI before submission) is organisational, not technical, and must be done before the manuscript cites a URL.

THE FROZEN NETWORK LAYOUT WILL NOT REPRODUCE PUBLISHED FIG 3e: no node-level coordinates exist anywhere on disk, and averaging the per-pair UMAP does not separate M1/M2/M5/M6 (centroid gaps are smaller than within-module spread). A build-time igraph layout is reproducible and stable but will look like a sibling of the figure, not the figure. A reader comparing the two side by side may think one of them is wrong; the 'featured (as published)' 52-node view and an explicit note are the mitigation.

THE FIG 3c UMAP COORDINATES LIVE OUTSIDE THE V4 PIPELINE: cca_winner_umap.npy sits in the sequence_analysis_v3_0515 tree, is regenerated by nothing in the v4 analysis, and cannot be recomputed to match the published figure. If that directory is ever cleaned up the pair explorer silently loses its input. The manifest records the path, size, mtime and SHA-256, and the quantized copy is committed to the portal snapshot, but the underlying provenance is fragile.

PROTEIN 'MOTIFS' CAN BE 535 aa LONG: protein motif_length has median 8 but maximum 535, so a single highlight can cover most of a protein and the word 'motif' becomes misleading at that end of the distribution. The span renderer must handle a highlight that spans dozens of read-mode lines, and the UI should surface motif_length as a filter. UTR motifs are capped at 55 and need no such handling.

RBP NAMES ARE NOT NORMALIZED AND NO ALIAS TABLE EXISTS: the 203 POSTAR3 labels include U2AF65/U2AF2, TDP43/TARDBP, UNR/CSDE1, IMP3/IGF2BP3, HNRNPH/HNRNPH1 and two opaque labels ('ACI', 4,960 entries; 'SDOS'). Without a hand-curated ~15-row alias map any RBP facet double-counts the same protein and splits evidence across method columns. The map is an afternoon of work but it is work nobody has done, and it is not derivable from any file in the tree.

NO PHYSICAL-INTERACTION EVIDENCE EXISTS ANYWHERE, SO EVERY LABEL IS A MISREADING RISK: every association in the portal is co-occurrence of motif clusters across genes, and the manuscript's own SRSF3/4 and PTBP attributions for utr5_0096 and utr3_0215 are literature inferences with no enrichment row in the data. The mitigation is structural (naming the field 'co-occurrence' in the data model so no template can emit 'binds', showing n_indep_clades and frac_co_ZNF inline on every edge, and separating 'evidence in this dataset' badges from 'author inference' badges) but it depends on discipline being maintained through every future template edit.

SHARD SIZE TOTALS ARE EXTRAPOLATED FROM SAMPLES, NOT FULL BUILDS: my core gene shard (3,514 B mean), annotation shard (681 B mean) and cluster shard (19,877 B mean) figures come from 400-transcript and 60-cluster samples respectively; the survey's own full 18,093-shard build measured 61.3 MB for a shard set without sequences or NTScore, which is consistent, but the ~100 MB total is an extrapolation until the first full build runs. If it lands materially higher, the top-200-member cluster variant (4.5 MB instead of 17.9 MB) and lazy annotation loading are the levers.

NO DELTA-ATTENTION MATRICES ARE STORED, SO THE PORTAL CANNOT SHOW WHY A REGION WAS CALLED: Fig 3a is drawn from synthetic data and PANELS.md says so. The most compelling possible addition for the reviewer audience — the actual attribution behind a highlight — would require rerunning MIRTO inference on a GPU and is out of scope for a static build. The methods diagram must label that step as schematic rather than implying the portal displays real attention.

THE PROTEIN PANEL IS PERMANENTLY ASYMMETRIC WITH THE UTR PANELS: per-nucleotide NTScore exists for 5'UTR and 3'UTR only (I verified both h5 files cover all 18,093 transcripts with exact length alignment), and there is no CDS or per-residue protein score anywhere. pLDDT as a per-motif bar is a genuine substitute for the IDR story but it is not the same quantity, and the gene page will look lopsided. This must be stated on the page rather than papered over.

SEARCH COVERS SYMBOLS AND IDS BUT NOT ALIASES: the index is built from the 17,847 gene_symbol values in the motif table; no alias or previous-symbol table was established by any survey, so a reader typing an older or alternative symbol gets nothing. A fuzzy fallback (trigram or Levenshtein over the 17,847 symbols, entirely client-side) mitigates typos but not genuine synonyms.

name: MIRTO Motifome Explorer
one_liner: A query-backed portal over the 889,215-instance bilingual motifome: a FastAPI + DuckDB analytical API serving per-nucleotide NTScore tracks, arbitrary boolean co-occurrence over 541,746 gene×cluster memberships, and on-the-fly enrichment against any gene set — behind a React/d3 front end that reads a transcript, a motif cluster, and the six-module network as one linked object.
stack:
BACKEND (all versions verified on this machine unless noted). Python 3.11 (/opt/anaconda3/envs/bio/bin/python). DuckDB 1.5.5 — NOT currently installed (`ModuleNotFoundError` on all four interpreters); `pip install duckdb` fetched 1.5.5 cleanly into a scratch target and I built and benchmarked the real database with it. pyarrow 21.0.0 (already present) for the build step only. h5py 3.x for the NTScore HDF5 caches. FastAPI 0.115 + uvicorn 0.32 (ASGI) under gunicorn with 2–4 uvicorn workers. pydantic v2.9 for typed request/response models (the filter AST is a pydantic discriminated union, never a raw SQL string). orjson 3.10 as the FastAPI response class — the R1 payload is float-array heavy and orjson serializes numpy natively. numpy 2.x + scipy 1.14 (`scipy.stats.hypergeom.sf`) for on-the-fly enrichment p-values; `statsmodels` 0.14 `multipletests` for BH FDR. pandas 2.x is used ONLY in the offline build script, never at request time.

DATA ENGINE. One embedded DuckDB file, opened read-only, with one `con.cursor()` per request (measured: 16 sequential cursors = 23.3 ms total, RSS 161 MB). Measured build: 2.4 s from the two source parquets, 225.5 MB on disk, 889,215 motif rows / 19,210 transcripts / 541,746 distinct (transcript, cluster) memberships. Indexes on `motif(gene_symbol)`, `motif(cluster)`, `motif(sequence_id)`, `gene_cluster(cluster)`, `gene_cluster(sequence_id)`, `tx(sequence_id)`. No external DBMS, no ORM, no connection pool to operate.

FRONTEND. TypeScript 5.6 + Vite 5 + React 18.3. TanStack Query v5 for all server state (request dedup, caching, `keepPreviousData` for paged tables, prefetch-on-hover for cluster popovers). TanStack Table v8 + TanStack Virtual v3 for every long table (cluster instance lists reach 5,755 rows; the pair grid reaches 180,000). d3 v7 as modules only — `d3-force`, `d3-scale`, `d3-shape`, `d3-zoom`, `d3-quadtree`, `d3-array`, `d3-axis`; no `d3-selection` DOM ownership (React owns the DOM, d3 computes). Zustand v5 for filter state, mirrored into the URL query string so every view is permalinkable. `wouter` for routing. Sequence logos are a ~120-line custom SVG renderer over the STREME PWM arrays — no logo library. No Plotly (the author's 9.56 MB inlined-Plotly prototype at sequence_analysis_v3_0515/04.visualize_motif_interaction/03.build_annotated_plotly_graph.py is the thing this replaces).

RENDER TECH BY SCALE. SVG for the sequence tracks (max 381 motif-or-gap segments per transcript page, measured) and for the 519-node/2,620-edge network (keeps hit-testing, focus rings, CSS hover free). Canvas 2D + d3-quadtree hit-testing for the 180,000-point Fig 3c UMAP — SVG is not an option there. HTML/CSS for the monospace sequence pane so text selection and copy work.

STYLING. CSS custom properties lifted from `_shared/manuscript_style.py` PALETTE (Okabe-Ito) and the three-state light/dark token block from `manuscript/results_code_mapping_index/03.panel_code_index.html`. Module colors follow the four-script `MCOL` used in the published Fig 3d/3e/ED3b: M1 #0072B2, M2 #CC79A7, M3 #E69F00, M4 #D55E00, M5 #4D4D4D, M6 #009E73 — explicitly overriding the conflicting `CATEGORICAL`-cycle variant in motif_umap/make_individual_figures.py and the never-implemented proposal in _shared/COLOR_TABLE.md.

DEPLOY. Multi-stage Docker (node:20 build → python:3.11-slim runtime), data baked into the image as an immutable layer. Google Cloud Run, 1 vCPU / 1 GiB, min-instances=1. Cloudflare in front for CDN + TLS on an institutional custom domain.
architecture:
DATA FLOW, parquet to pixels, in four hops.

HOP 1 — OFFLINE BAKE (`code/build/bake.py`, one idempotent script, ~15 min). Reads absolute paths under /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design and writes one relocatable output directory `dist/data/`. It emits (a) `portal.duckdb`, (b) `ntscore_utr3.h5` and `ntscore_utr5.h5` copied verbatim, (c) `pwm.json`, (d) `layout.json` with frozen node coordinates, (e) `manifest.json` with SHA-256 + mtime + source path of every input. Nothing downstream ever touches the original trees. Measured: the DuckDB half of this is 2.4 s; the STREME gap-fill is the long pole at ~15 min at WORKERS=10 (per survey [clusters], not re-verified by me).

HOP 2 — REQUEST. Browser → Cloudflare → Cloud Run → gunicorn → uvicorn worker → FastAPI route → pydantic-validated params → a parameterized DuckDB query on a per-request cursor, or an h5py group read. Two long-lived handles per worker process, opened at startup and warmed: `duckdb.connect(read_only=True)` and the two `h5py.File` handles. Warming matters — the FIRST h5 group read cost 349.5 ms (h5py builds its link index), every subsequent random read cost 0.20–0.29 ms. Startup therefore touches one key in each file before the health check goes green.

HOP 3 — SERIALIZATION. orjson for JSON. NTScore has a second, binary path: `Accept: application/octet-stream` returns raw float32, or `?encoding=u8` returns uint8 quantized over a fixed [-5, 0] domain with the scale in a response header. Measured on NOTCH1's 1,638-nt 3'UTR: JSON 12,892 B (gzip 3,333 B) vs uint8 1,638 B (gzip 1,477 B), max quantization error 0.0196 over an actual range of -3.812..-0.049. Worst case sampled across 4,000 transcripts was NM_000997 at 7,242 nt → ~13.3 KB gzipped JSON. JSON is the default because even the worst case is cheap; the binary path exists for the minimap that fetches many tracks at once.

HOP 4 — CLIENT. TanStack Query caches by URL. The transcript view composes one `GET /transcripts/{id}` (measured end-to-end, sequences + motifs + both NTScore tracks: ACTB 16.7 KB, SOX2 37.3 KB, NOTCH1 52.3 KB uncompressed JSON, 3–13 ms server time) plus lazy sub-requests for the domain/UniProt/RBP-peak tracks. React renders SVG tracks; d3 computes scales and the force layout.

MEASURED LATENCY OF THE WHOLE PROMISED SURFACE (min of 5, warm, single connection, this laptop):
  gene → all motifs (TP53, 34 rows)                     1.0 ms
  transcript → three sequences                          0.2 ms
  cluster → all members (utr3_0215, 566 rows)          11.9 ms
  CO-OCCURRENCE utr5_0079 ∧ prot_0072 → 51 tx           3.4 ms
  CO-OCCURRENCE utr5_0004 ∧ prot_0040 → 173 genes       4.3 ms
  BOOLEAN A ∧ B ∧ ¬C → 79 genes                        28.8 ms
  FACET ELAVL1 PAR-CLIP ∧ utr3 ∧ score>-0.5 → 5,390     4.4 ms
  FACET substring 'TCTCC' in utr3 → 6,767 genes         11.7 ms
  FACET protein ∧ plddt<0.4 ∧ has InterPro → 18,822     3.2 ms
  ON-THE-FLY ENRICHMENT, eCLIP over arbitrary tx set    13.2 ms
  RBP tally within one cluster                           1.8 ms
  GROUP BY over all 900 clusters                        11.2 ms
  autocomplete prefix (TP/SOX/HNRN/ZN)               3.7–7.4 ms
Nothing in the promised analytical surface exceeds 29 ms.

CORRECTNESS BUILT INTO THE BAKE. Two known upstream bugs are fixed in the CREATE TABLE, not in the UI. (1) The MobiDB/IDPO/SignalP region leak — `CASE WHEN region='protein' THEN ...` on all six protein-layer columns. I verified the fix: `SELECT count(*) FROM motif WHERE region<>'protein' AND mobidb IS NOT NULL` returns 0, against 209,959 spurious MobiDB rows in the source. (2) Transcript-table duplicates — `SELECT DISTINCT ON (refseq_id_without_ver)` collapses 21,667 rows to 19,210; survey [scale] verified all 1,296 duplicate groups are byte-identical so this is lossless. Coordinates are stored and served as 0-based, both-ends INCLUSIVE, and the constant lives in one place: JS `seq.slice(m.s, m.e + 1)`.

SECURITY POSTURE OF THE ANALYTICAL ENDPOINTS. `POST /query/*` accepts a pydantic discriminated-union filter AST (node types: `cluster`, `module`, `rbp`, `mirna`, `interpro`, `region`, `score_range`, `plddt_range`, `substring`, `and`, `or`, `not`) which a compiler turns into a parameterized SQL statement. Raw SQL is never accepted from the client. Guards: AST depth ≤ 6, ≤ 24 leaf terms, DuckDB `SET memory_limit='512MB'` and a 5-second statement timeout per cursor, per-IP rate limit (60 req/min, 10 req/min on POST /query/*) via slowapi, and a 50,000-row response cap with a cursor token for continuation.

DUAL-TARGET GUARANTEE. The same bake script has an `--emit-static` mode that walks the same route handlers offline and writes their JSON to a directory tree matching the API paths. That produces the archival fallback described in `tradeoffs` — the front end flips to it by changing one base URL. This is what makes a live backend a defensible choice for a paper rather than a liability.

Hover a point -> tooltip with both cluster ids, phylo_corrected_score, npmi_mip_APC, co_count, n_indep_clades, frac_co_ZNF

Dragging the 0.10 marker on the histogram re-colors the scatter live; the raw-NPMI axis is available but sorting the table by npmi_raw shows an inline warning naming the 25/30 ZNF artifact result

views.title: Query Workbench
views.purpose: The reason this architecture has a backend. Compose arbitrary boolean set queries over motif clusters, modules, RBPs, miRNAs, InterPro terms, regions and score ranges; get the transcript set back; and run enrichment on that set against any annotation vocabulary — none of which is answerable from pre-baked shards.
views.layout:
Three stacked bands: the AST builder on top, the result set in the middle, the derived analyses at the bottom. Deliberately dense and tool-like rather than editorial.

+==========================================================================+
| < Workbench                        [save] [permalink] [show SQL] [reset] |
+==========================================================================+
| BUILD A SET                                                              |
| +----------------------------------------------------------------------+ |
| | AND  v                                                               | |
| |  |- [cluster] utr5_0079            in 5'UTR         [x]  -> 538 tx  | |
| |  |- [cluster] prot_0072            in protein       [x]  -> 263 tx  | |
| |  |- NOT v                                                           | |
| |  |    |- [rbp] ELAVL1  methods:[PAR-CLIP][any]      [x]  -> 6,204   | |
| |  |- [score] motif_score >= -1.0                     [x]             | |
| |  [+ cluster] [+ module] [+ RBP] [+ miRNA] [+ InterPro] [+ region]   | |
| |  [+ substring] [+ pLDDT range] [+ AND/OR/NOT group]                 | |
| +----------------------------------------------------------------------+ |
|                             [ RUN ]   depth 2/6, 4 terms/24, est <30 ms |
+==========================================================================+
| RESULT  47 transcripts / 47 genes            [UpSet of the 4 terms]      |
| +-------------------------+  +----------------------------------------+  |
| | gene   tx        m5 m3 p |  |  utr5_0079 #########                   |  |
| | HNRNPD NM_002138  2  7  3|  |  prot_0072 ######                      |  |
| | HNRNPR NM_005826  1  9  2|  |  both      ###                         |  |
| | DDX17  NM_006386  3  4  4|  |  both - ELAVL1  ##                     |  |
| | ... [virtualized]        |  +----------------------------------------+  |
| +-------------------------+                                              |
| [export set: CSV | gene list | FASTA | to transcript view]               |
+==========================================================================+
| ENRICH THIS SET                                                          |
| vocabulary: [eCLIP v] universe: [all utr3-motif transcripts (18,006) v]  |
| test: hypergeometric, BH-corrected                          [ RUN ]      |
|                                                                          |
| term      k    n     K      N       fold    p        FDR                 |
| SLBP      23   196   41     18,006  51.5    5e-33    1e-30   [lollipop]  |
| GNL3       5    66   ...     ...     7.0    ...      ...                 |
| KHDRBS1    4    74   ...     ...     5.0    ...      ...                 |
| (!) Universe differs from the published gene-level table; see [methods]  |
+==========================================================================+

Every leaf term shows its own cardinality as you build, so a user sees a set collapse to zero before running the whole query. The [show SQL] panel prints the compiled, parameterized statement read-only — for transparency and for users who want to reproduce it against the published DuckDB file, not as an input.
interactions: Each leaf term resolves its own count on blur (a cheap COUNT query, measured 3–12 ms) so the builder gives feedback before RUN
RUN posts the AST to POST /query/cooccurrence; the compiled SQL is parameterized and never accepts client SQL
The UpSet panel is computed from the same response — one intersection-size vector over the leaf terms, so a user can see which term is doing the work
Result rows link to /t/{sequence_id}; 'to transcript view' opens the first hit with all AST clusters pre-highlighted

The enrichment band accepts the result set OR a pasted gene list (up to 5,000 symbols), and any of the annotation vocabularies (eCLIP, PAR-CLIP, iCLIP-P, iCLIP-C, miRNA, InterPro, MobiDB curated-only, ELM, IDPO, UniProt feature type)
Universe selector matters and says so: transcript-level vs the published gene-level universe give different numbers, and the panel prints which one produced the result
[permalink] serializes the AST into the URL (base64url of the JSON) so a query is citable in a paper or a reviewer reply
Guardrails surface as UI, not errors: exceeding depth 6 or 24 leaf terms disables [+], and a query that would exceed the 5 s statement timeout is refused with the estimated cost shown
views.entry_points: Arrives from: 'find genes like this' in the transcript inspector, 'find co-carriers' on a cluster partner row, 'open genes in workbench' from an edge drawer, a brushed selection in the pair explorer, or directly from global chrome. URL `/workbench?ast={base64url}`. Leaves to: /t/{id} from any result row, /c/{id} from any cluster chip, and CSV/FASTA downloads.
